label: French Cuff — 4 Buttonholes
note: Owner-uploaded reference images. Authoritative for construction/appearance; NOT usable as the tech-pack illustration (not line art, or shows multiple options).

references.evidence: Real photograph (208x260 px) of a worn pale-blue shirt cuff held between thumb and fingers. Closure is a single round pave/marcasite CUFFLINK head passing through the cuff; there are no buttons on the cuff itself (the two beige buttons at frame left sit on the shirt's front placket, not the cuff). A second fabric layer peeks past the wrist edge beside the thumb, consistent with a folded-back double cuff. Because the fastened cufflink covers the holes, ZERO buttonholes are countable - 4 vs 6 vs 8 cannot be distinguished.

Studio photograph (202x253 px) of a model's arm in a pale-blue shirt against dark trousers. The cuff is fastened by a single round silver cufflink head and carries no buttons, so it is a link cuff. The cuff reads as a deep squared panel, but the fold at the wrist edge that separates a double/French cuff from a single link cuff is not resolvable at this resolution, and the buttonholes are covered by the cufflink so none can be counted.
